sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from $70.3 billion in FY2016 to $104.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F205], but the path was a step change, not a smooth climb.
Revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021 [D183][D230], then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 surge came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase and new stores, with the pandemic shifting category and channel mix [P51][P55].
The recent decline reflects a 2.6% comparable sales decrease in FY2025, driven by a 2.2% traffic decline and a 0.4% lower average transaction [P14].
Merchandise sales were 98.0% of revenue in FY2025 and contributed -2.0pp to that year's decline [D465][D467].
Food & beverage grew 1.3% in FY2025 and added 0.3pp, while apparel fell 4.7% and subtracted 0.7pp [D507][D508][D564][D565].
The FY2023 sales decline came primarily from the Discretionary categories (Apparel & Accessories, Hardlines, Home Furnishings & Decor), partly offset by Frequency categories [P30].
Operating income grew 0.6% a year over the window against 4.5% revenue growth [F207][F205], and in FY2025 operating costs grew 0.4pp faster than revenue [D439].
Diluted EPS compounded at 6.3% against 3.4% net income growth [F210][F208], helped by a 1.3% lower diluted share count in FY2025 [D434].
The FY2025 operating margin of 4.9% sat below the 5.6% window median and well below the 8.4% FY2021 high [F34][D590][D589].
The 0.3pp operating-margin decline in FY2025 came from a 0.3pp cost-of-revenue effect, partly offset by a 0.1pp SG&A benefit [D429][D440][D441].

The gross margin rate fell to 27.9% from 28.2% on the net impact of several items [P12], and the SG&A rate held at 20.6% with a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit offset by 0.2pp of transformation costs [P11].
In FY2025 net margin of 3.5% sat 1.3pp below the 4.9% operating margin [F54][F34][D629], with a 22.3% effective tax rate [D403].
Operating cash flow of $6.56 billion was 1.77x net income in FY2025, below the 2.01x window median [F84][F44][D404][D619].
The FY2025 operating cash flow decrease reflects lower net earnings and the net impact of lower accounts payable leverage and inventory purchases [P7].
Free cash flow fell to $2.84 billion, a 2.7% margin against the 4.5% window median [F104][D401][D596], as capex of $3.73 billion ran at 1.19x D&A [F94][D406].
The FY2025 capex increase primarily reflects increased investment in both new stores and remodels [P5].
Cash of $5.49 billion against long-term debt of $14.4 billion leaves the company in net debt [F144][F194].
The current ratio was 0.94x, in line with the 0.94x window median [F184][D602], and return on average equity of 24.0% was below the 28.6% peer median (n=5) [D415][D617].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D412][D413], with repurchases down to $408 million [X126].
The diluted share count fell 1.3% in FY2025 [D434], extending a steady reduction from 582.5 million shares in FY2016 [X107].
Revenue declined in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, from $109.1 billion to $104.8 billion [R1][F7][F10].
Three straight down years on a shrinking store base is the central risk, and the FY2025 traffic decline points to demand rather than mix alone [P14].
The current ratio was 0.94x in FY2025, below 1.0x [R2][F184].
A sub-1.0x current ratio is normal for this retailer and matches its own median, so it is not a liquidity concern [D602].
The pack's liquidity and debt figures carry a data break: short-term investments sit inside cash, and the current debt portion sits inside long-term debt for FY2016-FY2018 [R7][R8].
Net cash and total-debt comparisons across those years are therefore not reliable, and this analysis avoids building conclusions on them.
Whether the operating margin holds above the 4.9% FY2025 level or slips toward the 3.5% FY2022 low [F34][D588], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 4.5% window median from 2.7% [D401][D596], with capex guided at approximately $5 billion for 2026 [P4].
Whether revenue growth turns positive from the -1.7% FY2025 rate [D416], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
